ORPHANED BY THE CHIEF'S OWN SLICE PLAN, found by checking that the six slices cover all 80 forgeable types. They did not. Three modules - amr-interop, proposition, story - appeared in NO slice, because the plan was sliced by module and the module list was derived from the 45-validating subset, so any module whose types are guarded externally or by phantom parameters fell out. This is the SECOND gap of the same origin; the first was codec.

THE THREE, and they are the strongest instances in the sweep:

AmrGraph[C <: CheckState, R <: RoleForm] private[amr] (AmrGraph.scala:16). Its Scaladoc states the guarantee outright: "Why a phantom-typed single class: downstream code can demand AmrGraph[Checked, CanonicalRoles] and be GUARANTEED that dangling references, missing concepts, and inverse spellings are gone", and "Construction is private: unchecked graphs come from AmrGraph.unchecked or the decoder; CHECKED GRAPHS ONLY FROM AmrValidator." fromProduct mints an AmrGraph[Checked, CanonicalRoles] that never saw AmrValidator.

PropositionChart[C <: CheckState] private[proposition] (chart.scala:252). Same phantom mechanism. Note document/mention.scala carries Map[SurfaceUnitId, PropositionChart[Checked]] - the Checked witness is already load-bearing downstream.

StoryModel[S <: ModelStatus] private[story] (model.scala:18). "Constructed only through StoryModel.draft and promoted by validation." fromProduct mints a StoryModel[Validated] that was never validated.

WHY THESE ARE WORSE THAN AN ORDINARY FORGE. For a phantom-typed class the Mirror can be summoned AT ANY TYPE ARGUMENT - Mirror.ProductOf[AmrGraph[Checked, CanonicalRoles]] - so the forger does not merely bypass validation, THE FORGER CHOOSES WHICH VALIDATION STATE TO CLAIM. And this is the mechanism design-contract rule 8 names as one of the thirteen non-negotiables: "Smart constructors + phantom states. Invalid states are unrepresentable when rules are stable (Checked/Unchecked, Draft/Validated)." That sentence is false for all three.

CRITERION APPLIED: none is saved. Their fields are ordinary data - NodeId, Vector, Map, Concept, Edge, StorySource, SurfaceAtlas - all obtainable, none unforgeable. No payload protects them the way PseudonymizedText protects AuthorizedRemoteRequest.

REQUIRED IN THE DEMONSTRATION: forge at a CHECKED type argument specifically, not a bare one - the point is not that a graph can be built, it is that a graph asserting it was validated can be built without validation.
